pixel_id.description: Snapchat Pixel ID is embedded directly in the API endpoint URL path. Both platforms derive it from destination configuration. For WEB events, a Pixel ID is required; for MOBILE_APP events, a Snap App ID is used instead.

access_token.description: Static long-lived access token passed as a URL query parameter. Generated in Snapchat Business Manager under Business Details > Conversions API Tokens.

event_name_mapping.description: Maps Segment/RudderStack event names to Snapchat standard event names. Both platforms apply similar transformations via their Transformer services.
event_name_mapping.custom_events: Non-standard event names can be mapped to CUSTOM_EVENT_1 through CUSTOM_EVENT_5 (maximum 5 custom event types supported by Snapchat)

email.transform: Lowercase, trim whitespace, SHA-256 hash. Snapchat accepts an array of hashed values.
email.description: Email address is lowercased, trimmed, and SHA-256 hashed before sending to Snapchat. The em field is an array to support multiple email addresses.

phone.transform: Remove all non-numeric characters except leading +, then SHA-256 hash. Snapchat accepts an array of hashed values.
phone.description: Phone number is normalized (remove spaces, dashes, parentheses) and SHA-256 hashed before sending to Snapchat. The ph field is an array to support multiple phone numbers.

external_id.description: A unique user identifier (typically userId) is SHA-256 hashed and sent as external_id. Used for cross-platform user matching when Snap Pixel cookie is unavailable.

sc_click_id.segment_source: Extracted from page URL query parameter 'ScCid' or context.integrations.Snapchat.scClickId
sc_click_id.rudderstack_source: Extracted from page URL query parameter 'ScCid' or context.integrations.Snapchat.scClickId
sc_click_id.description: Snapchat Click ID (ScCid) is extracted from the ad landing page URL and forwarded for ad attribution. When a user swipes on a Snap ad, the ScCid parameter is appended to the destination URL. Can also be sent via event_source_url for automatic extraction.

sc_cookie1.description: Snap Pixel first-party cookie identifier (_scid). Used to associate server-side events with Snap Pixel browser events for improved matching. If Snap Pixel is implemented on the site, this cookie is set automatically.

ip_address.description: Client IP address forwarded for geo-targeting and user matching.

user_agent.description: Browser user agent string forwarded for device identification and matching.

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency code. Required for PURCHASE events.

value.description: Monetary value of the event as a string. Required for PURCHASE events. Segment and RudderStack both map revenue/value/total to Snapchat value.

transaction_id.description: Order or transaction identifier. Also used as a deduplication key with a 30-day window for PURCHASE events.

contents.description: Product array mapped from Segment spec products to Snapchat contents format. Used for custom conversions value and ROAS reporting.

item_mappings.name: Not directly mapped in Snapchat contents; use item_ids for identification

item_ids.description: Array of product IDs from the products array. Provides a flat list of SKU/product identifiers.

num_items.description: Count of distinct items in the event.

search_string.description: Search query string for SEARCH events.

description.description: A freeform text description for additional context.

event_tag.description: Custom label to tag events for additional segmentation in Snapchat Ads Manager.

brands.description: Brands associated with item_ids in the conversion event.

level.description: Level reached in a game or app (for gaming/app events).

event_name.segment_source: Derived from event type mapping (track event name → Snapchat standard event name)
event_name.rudderstack_source: Derived from event type mapping (track event name → Snapchat standard event name)
event_name.description: Snapchat standard event name in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE format (e.g., PURCHASE, PAGE_VIEW, ADD_CART).

event_time.segment_source: timestamp (ISO 8601 converted to Unix epoch seconds)
event_time.rudderstack_source: timestamp (ISO 8601 converted to Unix epoch seconds)
event_time.description: Event timestamp as Unix epoch seconds (integer). Both platforms must convert ISO 8601 timestamp to epoch seconds. Events can be up to 37 days old to be eligible for attribution.

event_id.description: Unique event identifier used for deduplication between Snap Pixel and CAPI events. Deduplication occurs on event_id and timestamp within a 48-hour window.

client_dedup_id.description: Client-side deduplication ID. Provides a 48-hour deduplication window. Should match across all integrations (Snap Pixel, third party, or direct CAPI calls).

action_source.segment_source: Defaults to 'WEB'; derived from event context (mobile → 'MOBILE_APP', offline → 'OFFLINE')
action_source.rudderstack_source: Defaults to 'WEB'; configurable per destination settings (eventConversionType)
action_source.description: Supported values: WEB, MOBILE_APP, OFFLINE. Determines the event channel type. WEB requires a Pixel ID, MOBILE_APP requires a Snap App ID.

event_source_url.description: Full page URL where the event occurred. Snapchat can automatically extract the ScCid (Click ID) from this URL if present as a query parameter.

known_differences.description: Segment uses 'analytics.js'; RudderStack uses 'rudder-sdk-js'. This field is in the input event and does not affect the Snapchat output payload.
known_differences.impact: No impact — library metadata is not forwarded to Snapchat.

known_differences.description: RudderStack input events include additional fields: rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt. These are RudderStack-specific envelope fields not present in Segment events.
known_differences.impact: No impact — these envelope fields are not forwarded to Snapchat.

known_differences.description: Segment and RudderStack generate messageId values using different UUID strategies. Both are used as event_id and client_dedup_id for Snapchat deduplication.
known_differences.impact: Minimal — only affects deduplication key format, not functionality. Deduplication still works within each platform.

known_differences.description: Both platforms should extract the Snapchat Click ID (ScCid) from the page URL query parameter. Verify URL parsing handles edge cases identically (encoded characters, missing parameter, case sensitivity).
known_differences.impact: Could affect ad attribution if Click ID extraction logic differs between platforms.

known_differences.description: Both platforms should SHA-256 hash email (lowercase, trim), phone (strip non-numeric except leading +), and external_id. Verify normalization steps are identical before hashing.
known_differences.impact: Different normalization produces different hashes, affecting Snapchat user matching rates. Snapchat requires lowercase hex SHA-256 format.

known_differences.description: Snapchat CAPI v3 requires event_time as Unix epoch seconds (integer). Both platforms must convert ISO 8601 timestamps. Verify timezone handling and rounding behavior are consistent.
known_differences.impact: Incorrect timestamps affect event attribution windows and deduplication.

known_differences.description: Verify that the Transformer service maps Segment spec event names to Snapchat standard event names identically between Segment and RudderStack. Snapchat only supports 22 standard events plus 5 custom events.
known_differences.impact: Different event name mappings cause events to be categorized differently in Snapchat Ads Manager.

known_differences.description: Snapchat CAPI expects value as a string type. Verify both platforms convert numeric revenue values to strings consistently.
known_differences.impact: Type mismatch could cause validation failures or incorrect ROAS reporting.

known_differences.description: Snap Pixel sets a _scid first-party cookie. Both platforms must extract and forward this cookie value for improved matching. Verify cookie extraction methods are consistent.
known_differences.impact: Missing sc_cookie1 reduces matching performance but events are still processed.

validation_requirements: Verify pixel_id is correctly embedded in the API URL path from destination config
Verify access_token is correctly passed as a query parameter
Verify all standard event name mappings match Segment's Snapchat destination
Verify PII fields (email, phone, external_id) are SHA-256 hashed with identical normalization (lowercase hex format)
Verify ScCid (Click ID) extraction from URL query parameters matches Segment behavior
Verify sc_cookie1 (_scid) cookie value forwarding matches Segment behavior
Verify contents[] array mapping from products[] is field-for-field identical
Verify event_time is converted from ISO 8601 to Unix epoch seconds correctly
Verify event_id and client_dedup_id use messageId consistently for deduplication
Verify action_source (WEB/MOBILE_APP/OFFLINE) is set correctly based on event context
Verify event_source_url is forwarded to allow automatic Click ID extraction
Verify custom_data.value is sent as a string type
Verify transaction_id is forwarded from order_id for 30-day PURCHASE deduplication
Verify non-standard events are mapped to CUSTOM_EVENT_1 through CUSTOM_EVENT_5
Verify batch request format wraps events in a top-level data array

notes: Snapchat is a shared cloud destination in the Advertising category. Segment has an Actions-based variant (actions-snap-conversions). RudderStack delivers Snapchat via the Router as a cloud REST destination. The Snapchat Conversions API v3 endpoint (https://tr.snapchat.com/v3/{pixel_id}/events) requires a Pixel ID in the URL path and an access_token as a query parameter. User data fields (em, ph, external_id) must be normalized and SHA-256 hashed (lowercase hex) before transmission. Snapchat supports event deduplication via client_dedup_id (48-hour window) and transaction_id (30-day window for PURCHASE events). Events are sent in a top-level data array supporting batch requests (up to 2000 events per batch). Key parity focus areas: event name mapping consistency (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE format), PII normalization and hashing, ScCid (Click ID) forwarding, sc_cookie1 cookie forwarding, event_time epoch conversion, contents/products array field mapping, and value type handling (string vs number). Snapchat CAPI v2 was deprecated in early 2025; v3 is the current supported version.
